decisions.reason: As a close extension of the service promise, the fifteen-day express program should be kept because management has already committed operational resources to it and can plausibly treat any weak early uptake as a temporary ramp-up issue in a growing market.

The seventy-two-hour express program should be kept because it reinforces the firm's fast-response positioning, likely required meaningful logistics commitment, and management would be inclined to justify that investment rather than reverse it after only a short time.

The fire-resistant steel exterior door should be kept because the homepage launch and European approval indicate strong public and technical commitment to a product that sits squarely in the firm's core safety-oriented business.

The express delivery program for doors and gates should be kept because a dedicated webpage signals visible commitment and it directly supports the firm's one-stop, reduced-downtime value proposition.

The online ordering and digital services platform should be kept because it likely involved substantial sunk IT and process investment and is central to the firm's stated move toward deeper advisory and service support on complex projects.

The fire and smoke protection door should be kept because it is closely aligned with the firm's established certified safety offer and any disappointing first-year results can credibly be attributed to long project cycles and adoption delays rather than a failed concept.
